fix_round.reason: An independent Opus review of the first pass found the isolation check's canary write actually landed in the LIVE production store (workspace/project agent-lab, wiki page 01a0b7ad-.../canary/test.md, git commit 9f9a01c, mtime 2026-09-22 20:24:58 -0400), because the CLI client commands defaulted to AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:49374 (the live service's port) -- only the isolated `serve`'s own `--bind`/config.toml were changed, not the client target. Every reported write/search/read/status result in the first-pass receipt therefore came from the live 2.3.2 service, not the isolated 2.4.0 build, and the receipt's 'live store unchanged' and 2.4.0-specific 'regression_finding' claims were both false. This is documented pre-existing ai-memory behavior, not new: evidence/artifacts/memory-lifecycle-probe-20260921/commands.json:583 shows the retained 2.3.2 probe explicitly setting AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL for exactly this reason.
fix_round.corrective_action: Re-ran the entire isolated check with a fresh data dir (data-v2), AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL pointed at the isolated server's own port, AI_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=none set both in the environment and in the isolated config.toml (avoiding the undisclosed ~87MB model download the first pass triggered), and an explicit --workspace/--project pair (sota-refresh-pins-mem/isolation-check-v2) distinct from the live service's agent-lab/agent-lab scope. Verified after the run, by direct filesystem/git-log inspection of $HOME/.local/share/ai-memory, that the live store's wiki tree gained no new canary page from this second pass (only the live service's own automatic lifecycle-hook session-observation capture recorded this session's shell activity, which is documented existing behavior, not a wiki write).
fix_round.stray_live_page_unresolved: The first pass's stray page $HOME/.local/share/ai-memory/wiki/<workspace-uuid>/<project-uuid>/canary/test.md (the agent-lab workspace/project scope's own wiki subdirectory UUIDs, found via `grep -rl canary $HOME/.local/share/ai-memory/wiki`; git commit 9f9a01c 'write-page agent-lab/agent-lab: canary/test.md') was NOT deleted by this unit: removing it was a destructive change to the live production store and, per the review and this unit's isolation contract (never touch a live service/store), was left for the coordinator or user to decide and execute. This receipt records the fact and the exact path/commit for that follow-up; it did not perform the deletion itself.
fix_round.coordinator_followup_deletion: RESOLVED at coordinator level, outside this unit's isolation scope: the coordinator deleted the stray canary/test.md page from the live agent-lab/agent-lab wiki scope through `memory_delete_page` on 2026-09-23 (wiki checkpoints ea02e38 -> e2fadf4). Per the #81 finding, this is a wiki-level delete, not byte-level erasure: the page and its history remain recoverable from the wiki git history (prior to e2fadf4) and from the live store's SQLite WAL. This is disclosed for the record; no further action on the stray page is expected from this unit.
fix_round.secret_exposure_disclosure: In the course of comparing config.toml files (both first-pass and this fix round), this session's transcript and command output included the live production ai-memory instance's `[auth] token_pepper` value in plaintext (from $HOME/.local/share/ai-memory/data/config.toml, read via `cat`/`grep` while diagnosing the isolation bug). Per the auth-token semantics documented in that same config file, `token_pepper` only affects the hash of native `aim_` API keys added after rotation (human password login is unaffected), so rotating it is a low-blast-radius, reversible action, but it is still a live secret this unit should not have needed to view and does not have authorization to rotate. Flagged for the user/coordinator to decide whether to rotate; not rotated by this unit.
fix_round.gitleaks: Re-ran on this worktree after the fix round: `gitleaks git . --config .gitleaks.toml --max-target-megabytes 2 --no-banner --exit-code 0 --log-opts=HEAD --report-format json` -> '397 commits scanned... no leaks found' (the first pass's 'blocked: another scan holds the per-user lock' was a transient contention with a concurrent sibling worker's scan, not a persistent failure).
